bull_bear.body: - Disciplined deal selection (all deals long-term margin-accretive); continued investment in talent/IP/software licenses, calibrated to growth. FCF +94% YoY (US$167mn), ROCE 28.3% — strong capital efficiency. Portfolio-company consolidation/liquidation of underperformers continues (SG&A benefit). No specific dividend/buyback commentary this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **European-auto pull-forward reversal** (~1–1.3% Q2 revenue drag) — must be offset by large-deal ramps + base performance.
- **Wage bill (Q2)** + **AI productivity pressure** on pricing — margin discipline "not taken for granted."
- **Comms volatility** — a large US telecom client volatile; cloud pass-through pullback (reverses Q2).
- **Competition "irrational"** on productivity/price guarantees — a demand-quality risk if TechM must match to win.
- **Memory/chip inflation ~20% YoY** — refuses to guarantee for 3–5-yr deals.
- **Client contract-signing delays** — one or two multi-year examples (in-house vs outsource, AI-benefit questions); mgmt says "not different from 25+ years" and no outsized cancellations. No ramp-up delays worth worrying about.
- **Demand-challenged areas:** manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM, legacy infra admin.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident but disciplined — "final year of transformation," proud of the journey, yet repeatedly refuses to give specific growth numbers ("foolhardy" / "hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two"), which reads as credible given large-deal binary-outcome candor. Mohit Joshi (25+ yrs industry) is precise on demand nuances (winners vs challenged areas) and openly names competitor "irrationality" with concrete examples. CFO Rohit Anand quantifies headwinds cleanly (European-auto 1–1.3% Q2). Overall: high-quality, numbers-grounded, low-hype.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Growth quality > the print:** the strong quarter was partly an auto pull-forward (~1–1.3%), so the "clean" run-rate is a touch lower — but every vertical grew YoY and the large-deal ramp (not yet started) is the real Q2+ driver.
- **The margin story is shifting composition:** Q1 expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius/FP-productivity/T&M-utilisation) are still largely UNSPENT — supportive of the 15% exit even against wage + AI-pricing headwinds.
- **Headcount down 7% YoY is NOT a demand signal** — it's AI-driven FP productivity + repurposing; hiring resumes in H2. Onsite-offshore pyramid lever is deferred (rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow) — a margin lever for LATER years, not FY27.
- **"SaaS eclipse" explicitly rejected** — enterprise-app (SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce) demand strengthening; a useful counter-read to bearish IT-services SaaS-disruption narratives.
- **AI is both opportunity and operating-model risk** — some traditional work compresses/needs new commercial constructs (token economics, AI FinOps, outcome-linked delivery) even as new demand expands.

bull_bear.body:
- Part of the Mahindra Group (founded 1945), one of the largest and most admired multinational federations of companies, providing brand lineage and ecosystem access.
- Full-stack, integrated service portfolio spanning consulting, IT, business process services, engineering, network services, customer experience & design, AI & analytics and cloud & infrastructure — cited as a core SWOT strength ('Full-stack service offerings').

- First Indian company awarded the Sustainable Markets Initiative's Terra Carta Seal; recognised as a Global Sustainability Leader in the S&P Global DJSI and the only Indian IT company with an 'A' rating across all three CDP categories (Climate Change, Water Security, Supplier Engagement).
- Industry-highest Net Promoter Score (NPS), cited by management as reflecting client trust.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Revenue growth stagnation / macro-demand risk — Reduced client spend from adverse business conditions, competitive loss, or global economic slowdown/recession — including geopolitical conflicts such as the Middle East wars, GDP/inflation/interest-rate headwinds and trade wars — could adversely impact revenue growth; management notes direct revenue exposure to affected regions is only a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue.
- Cyber security and data privacy risk — Risk of data theft, information-security deviations and cyber attacks; unauthorized use or disclosure of employee, company or customer data could breach customer contracts, trigger regulatory fines/penalties, or damage reputation.
- Impairment and M&A integration risk — Possibility of declining business performance at acquired portfolio companies, due to a weak economic environment or strategic/operational factors, leading to impairment; inability or delay in integrating acquisitions to achieve synergies could cause financial losses, reputational damage, reduced productivity or legal matters.
- Human capital risk — High attrition levels, involuntary churn, leadership/organisational change, and work-from-home productivity and data-security risks could adversely impact resource deployment on new and existing projects.
- Statutory compliance risk — Tracking constantly changing compliance requirements across multiple geographies and legal entities is a challenge; non-compliance could damage reputation or result in penal action by regulators.
- Technology risk (competency obsolescence) — Inability to timely adopt or invest in emerging technological competencies could create a competitive disadvantage; developing or acquiring new technologies and organisation-wide adoption carries significant cost implications.
- Delivery capability / capacity risk — Inherent project-level risk of not delivering on time, within budget, or to customer specifications, which could lead to penalties, loss of business, or reputational damage.
- Legal and contractual risk — Legal, litigation and contractual risk arising from contract execution and matters relating to IPR, tax, regulations, employment contracts, adverse rulings, and mergers.

- **Project Helix (AI-led transformation):** platforms + talent + partnerships in one operating model; agentic development & modernization services portfolio launched; TechM Orion (multi-agent orchestration) — 20+ agents on Google Gemini marketplace, 100+ active users; 350+ deployable AI agents; TechM Scale for vendor-consolidation.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- "AI Delivered Right" is TechM's core operating strategy — organising how delivery teams are structured and trained, how service lines invest, and how clients evaluate the company, built on four pillars: Transformation Delivered, Productivity Delivered, Innovation Delivered, and Assurance Delivered.
- TechM Orion, the company's enterprise-grade agentic AI platform, is the execution vehicle for the AI Delivered Right strategy, unifying agent design, orchestration, governance and scaling across the enterprise stack.
- Evolving commercial models for the AI era: 'Vector Squads' (composable delivery units of agents plus human experts priced by outcome, not headcount) and 'Service Tokens' (consumption-based commercial units for AI-led services) — a shift from billable hours to outcome/consumption pricing.
- Project Fortius continues to drive operational rigor through disciplined cost management, improved utilisation, optimised delivery structures, and enhanced billing realisation.
- Turbocharge program continues to drive disciplined account mining and execution across existing large accounts, with a differentiated operating approach focused on hygiene, performance, governance and reporting.
- Customer-centricity strategy anchored on the Must Have Accounts (MHA) program, using focused account playbooks for deeper CXO engagement, stronger solution mapping and accelerated new-logo acquisition in priority markets.
- Continued scale-up of investment in 'TechM Consulting' and Global Capability Centre (GCC)-related offerings, both cited as already delivering tangible business impact and strengthening strategic positioning.
- Large-scale workforce upskilling in AI and Generative AI (80,000+ associates enabled) to align talent capability with evolving client demand and embed AI within large transformation programs.
- Sustained focus on high-growth service lines, prioritised markets, disciplined capital allocation, and integration of acquired portfolio companies to advance toward FY27 profitability objectives under the FY27 roadmap.
- Continued expansion of the ESG-led service portfolio — ESG advisory and consulting, resource and energy management, EHS risk management, regulatory compliance and incident tracking, and supply-chain/ESG reporting platforms.
- Per its Dividend Distribution Policy (Regulation 43A, SEBI Listing Regulations), TechM commits to a minimum payout ratio of 85% or more of free cash flow generated over a five-year period, distributed as dividends and/or buybacks; the payout is determined based on available financial resources and investment requirements, reflecting a stated commitment to delivering shareholder value and optimal returns. For FY26 the Board confirmed an Interim Dividend of ₹15 per equity share (300% of face value, paid November 2025) and recommended a Final Dividend of ₹36 per equity share (720% of face value).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: As an asset-light global IT services and consulting business, TechM's 'expansion' in FY26 was expressed through capability and footprint build-out rather than physical plant capacity: deepening aerospace & defence capabilities within Manufacturing to offset automotive softness; scaling the BFSI portfolio-company offerings (payments, asset & wealth management, core banking, insurance platforms) and launching i.GreenFinance; continued investment scale-up in 'TechM Consulting' and Global Capability Centre (GCC)-related offerings; and integration of acquired portfolio companies across front-, middle- and back-office functions. On the sustainable-procurement side, TechM has set a goal to evaluate the top 250 of its high-spend key suppliers by 2030 for regulatory, ethical and sustainability compliance. Under BRSR Principle 2, the company disclosed that capital expenditure directed toward environmentally/socially beneficial technologies (infrastructure, energy and water efficiency initiatives) was 2.12% of total capex in FY26, down from 2.55% in FY25, while comparable R&D spend (AI, Cloud, Innovation and core R&D) rose to 33.2% of total R&D from 30% in FY25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural demand drivers — digital modernisation, cloud adoption, and AI-enabled transformation — continue to underpin medium-to-long-term IT services industry fundamentals even as near-term spending is more phased and prioritised.
- Enterprise GenAI adoption is maturing: interest remains strong but enterprises are more selective, prioritising use cases with clearer links to operational efficiency, cost optimisation and scalability; legacy-system modernisation for AI readiness is expected to expand the addressable market over time.
- Agentic AI is gaining momentum, with enterprises beginning to explore agent-based workflows for targeted efficiency improvements.
- Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are maturing beyond scale expansion toward higher-value, more integrated mandates, creating a continued partner role for IT services companies in governance frameworks, digital platforms and operating models.
- FY26 consolidated revenue growth was primarily driven by strong performance in the Manufacturing and BFSI verticals, with additional momentum from Retail, Travel and Logistics, supported by deeper engagement in existing accounts and ramp-up/scaling of new client wins.
- Communications vertical: multi-year strategic engagements entered with leading European telecommunications service providers focused on innovation, digital resilience and AI-led operational efficiencies; AI-led offerings are enhancing the company's 'right to win' with telecom clients.
- Manufacturing vertical: global automotive sector remains challenged, prompting a proactive shift toward aerospace and defence, construction, energy & utilities and mining, with focus on Industry 4.0, smart factory and IoT-enabled solutions.
- BFSI vertical: financial institutions remain focused on operational resilience while selectively advancing transformation programs tied to efficiency and risk management; niche strength in payments, asset & wealth management, core banking and insurance platforms.
- Industry outlook for FY26/FY27 reflects cautious optimism and a measured growth trajectory amid macroeconomic uncertainty and elevated tariffs; external industry advisors place FY27 IT-services growth expectations broadly in the 2-5% range.
- Direct revenue exposure to geopolitically affected regions (e.g. Middle East conflict zones) is a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue and is not expected to be material.
- Large deal bookings heading into FY27 are at their highest level in over a decade for TechM, reflecting a well-balanced mix across verticals and geographies.
- Total deal wins of USD 3.79 billion in FY26, a 42% year-on-year increase, including closure of large and strategic deals and continued diversification of revenue mix across markets, industries and service lines.
- Highest LTM (last-twelve-month) deal wins in a decade, even amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty.
- Top accounts continue to outpace overall organisational growth, supported by a robust pipeline driven through structured account planning, focused leadership interventions, and deep account-mining initiatives.
- $20 million+ accounts under the Turbocharge program are achieving quarterly run rates exceeding $1 billion and growing faster than the company average.

deepdive.thesis: The turnaround is delivering on schedule in its "final year": revenue US$1.66bn (+6.6% YoY CC), the strongest growth since the transformation began, with EVERY vertical growing YoY and manufacturing +17.2% YoY (aerospace + an accelerated European-auto program). Operating margin 14.4% (+330bps YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of expansion), TCV US$1.078bn (+33% YoY, third straight >$1bn), FCF +94% YoY, ROCE 28.3% (+450bps YoY). Management reaffirms the FY27 goalposts: growth above peer average (already achieved in Q1) and a 15% operating margin (exit Q4 >15%). Project Helix (agentic-AI, 350+ agents, Orion platform) is the growth engine; Project Fortius the margin engine. Near-term watch: a ~1–1.3% European-auto revenue pull-forward reverses in Q2, wage hikes land Q2, and AI productivity pressures pricing — but large-deal ramps are guided to offset.

risks.note: Reduced client spend from adverse business conditions, competitive loss, or global economic slowdown/recession — including geopolitical conflicts such as the Middle East wars, GDP/inflation/interest-rate headwinds and trade wars — could adversely impact revenue growth; management notes direct revenue exposure to affected regions is only a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue.

Risk of data theft, information-security deviations and cyber attacks; unauthorized use or disclosure of employee, company or customer data could breach customer contracts, trigger regulatory fines/penalties, or damage reputation.
risks.risk: Cyber security and data privacy risk

risks.note: Possibility of declining business performance at acquired portfolio companies, due to a weak economic environment or strategic/operational factors, leading to impairment; inability or delay in integrating acquisitions to achieve synergies could cause financial losses, reputational damage, reduced productivity or legal matters.

High attrition levels, involuntary churn, leadership/organisational change, and work-from-home productivity and data-security risks could adversely impact resource deployment on new and existing projects.
Tracking constantly changing compliance requirements across multiple geographies and legal entities is a challenge; non-compliance could damage reputation or result in penal action by regulators.

Inability to timely adopt or invest in emerging technological competencies could create a competitive disadvantage; developing or acquiring new technologies and organisation-wide adoption carries significant cost implications.
Inherent project-level risk of not delivering on time, within budget, or to customer specifications, which could lead to penalties, loss of business, or reputational damage.
Legal, litigation and contractual risk arising from contract execution and matters relating to IPR, tax, regulations, employment contracts, adverse rulings, and mergers.
